headline: On November 23, 2001: Budapest Convention on Cybercrime signed
captionCards: First treaty to harmonize national cybercrime laws
instagramCaption:
First global treaty to fight cybercrime was signed in Budapest.



Delegates from 44 nations gathered in Hungary to address digital crime. The treaty was drafted by the Council of Europe in Strasbourg, with participation from Canada, Japan, the Philippines, South Africa, and the United States. A surprising detail: it was the first international agreement to harmonize national laws on cybercrime. Its legacy lives on as a foundation for global digital law enforcement cooperation.
